summary: SimpleX Chat is an instant messaging platform built to operate without user identifiers like phone numbers or account numbers, using anonymous unidirectional queues instead. It provides end-to-end encrypted communication through custom application layers, keeping metadata hidden from intermediaries. The project is implemented in Haskell and distributed under the AGPL-3.0 licence.
goodFor: Privacy-focused individuals and technical teams who want to communicate without exposing transport metadata or relying on centralised account registries.
watchOut: Because it avoids standard identifiers and uses a decentralised queue architecture, setting it up for non-technical peers can be complex, and adoption heavily trails mainstream chat tools.
deployNotes: Hosting typically requires configuring a reverse proxy for TLS termination and ensuring persistent storage is mapped for message queues. Haskell applications generally run well inside lightweight container environments with adequate memory allocated for the runtime.
